definition: Trust in yourself, which he says collapses when you break promises you made to yourself.
example: How do you expect to have faith in yourself if you can't even keep your own word?

definition: Approval from other people, which he says we chase as a substitute for approving of ourselves.
example: We sacrifice the thing we want (self worth) for the thing which is supposed to get it (validation).

definition: Your own estimate of your value. He warns against parking it in other people's opinions.
example: You must not outsource your sense of self-worth or you will live at the mercy of everyone's opinion.

definition: To hand a task to someone else. He uses it for handing your self-respect to an audience.
example: You must not outsource your sense of self-worth or you will live at the mercy of everyone's opinion.

definition: Miserable and unfit. His word for other people's heads as a home for your self-worth.
example: Other people's heads are a wretched place for your self-worth to live.

definition: The fear that you are not enough. He says success can be a flight from that fear rather than a cure.
example: If your drive to succeed comes from a fear of insufficiency, and yet the feeling of insufficiency persists, what makes you think that the answer to this problem is more success?

definition: An empty place inside. External success, he says, will not fill it.
example: External success won't fill an internal void.

definition: Sharply conscious of something. He uses it for people who know the edge of what they know.
example: The smartest people I know are hyper-aware of the limits of their knowledge.

definition: The traits that make you unlike other people. He treats them as an advantage no rival can copy.
example: Your weirdness is your competitive advantage. No one can beat you at being you.

definition: Able to win against others. He locates the advantage in being irreducibly yourself.
example: Your weirdness is your competitive advantage.

definition: The feeling of wanting to act. He says the work does not wait for it.
example: You don't need motivation to do the thing. You just need to do the thing.

definition: The demand that conditions be ideal before you move. He calls it delay dressed up as care.
example: Perfectionism is procrastination masquerading as quality control.

definition: Putting off the action. In his line, it hides inside the claim that you are only protecting quality.
example: Perfectionism is procrastination masquerading as quality control.

definition: Appearing as something else. His verb for delay that pretends to be standards.
example: Perfectionism is procrastination masquerading as quality control.

definition: Standing still. He wants anxiety to trigger action instead of this.
example: If you feel anxiety creeping in, use it as a trigger to lean into action, not stagnation.

definition: A remedy that counters a poison. Action, he says, is the one for anxiety.
example: Action is the antidote to anxiety.

definition: Uneasy fear about what is coming. He treats it as a signal to move, not to freeze.
example: Action is the antidote to anxiety.

definition: Anxious, looping worries. He says they tax the journey more than they change the result.
example: Your fears and neuroses about them are doing little other than making your journey toward achieving them more miserable.

definition: Moral soundness. He says lying, by omission or commission, wears it down.
example: Whether by omission or commission, lying degrades your virtue.

definition: Leaving something out. He counts a lie by omission as a lie.
example: Whether by omission or commission, lying degrades your virtue.
